AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Herpes zoster (HZ) and postherpetic neuralgia are known to have a profound effect on the patient's quality of life, but the incidence and severity of itch and its relation with pain and quality of life in the long term are still relatively unknown.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The aim of this study was to measure the presence and severity of pain and itch and impact on quality of life in patients over 50 years old with HZ.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We enrolled 661 patients with HZ in this 12-month observational study. Patient data were collected via a web-based questionnaire. Outcomes were pain, itch, burden of illness, impact on patient's daily life, impact on quality of life, and healthcare costs.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: At inclusion, 94% of patients reported any pain, 74.3% significant pain, and 26% severe pain. After 3 months, 18.8% of patients suffered from postherpetic neuralgia. At inclusion, 70.8% of patients had any itch, 39.2% significant itch, and 7.3% severe itch. The occurrence of pain increases costs and has a high impact on the quality of life, lowering EQ-5D scores by an average of 18%. In contrast, itch has little effect on the quality of life.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Pain and itch are highly prevalent months after HZ. Pain caused by HZ has a large impact on quality of life, burden of illness, impact on daily life, and health care costs for these patients. The impact of itch on quality of life is relatively small.
